trip_plan.totalNote: Four days from Downey Creek: two days in to a high camp near the Dome Glacier, a climbing day on the north face, and a long day out.

days.title: Downey Creek to Itswoot Ridge
days.objective: Camp on Itswoot Ridge
days.note: Begin the approach shared with the Southwest Route, hiking from the Downey Creek Trailhead up Bachelor Creek to camp on Itswoot Ridge.

days.title: Move up to the Dome Glacier high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp near the Dome Glacier
days.note: Continue from Itswoot Ridge to a high camp near the Dome Glacier.

days.title: Climb the North Face
days.objective: Summit Sinister Peak via the north face
days.note: From high camp, cross the Dome-Chickamin col (about 8,500 ft), descend onto the Chickamin Glacier, and climb the north face directly to the summit. Return to camp.

days.title: Hike out to Downey Creek
days.objective: Return to the Downey Creek Trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach to the Downey Creek Trailhead; some parties take two days for this.

camps_on_file.name: Dome Glacier and Dome-Chickamin col high bivouacs
camps_on_file.notes: These are the camps that put the eastern peaks in range, and they are the reason parties carry a full glacier kit past Itswoot Ridge. The col between the Dana and Dome glaciers holds a couple of rock rings around 7,470 ft, and further east the Dome-Chickamin col is a genuine high camp with figures around 8,000 ft and a…

camps_on_file.name: Itswoot Ridge
camps_on_file.notes: This is the working base for the southern peaks and the camp most parties coming in from Downey Creek actually use. Camps are quoted anywhere between roughly 5,900 and 6,400 ft depending on which bench you take, so the number here describes the lower, wetter end of the ridge rather than a single spot. From the benches …

camps_on_file.name: Bachelor Creek forest and meadow camps
camps_on_file.notes: This exists because of the brush, and the brush is the single most important thing to understand about the south end. From the Downey Creek trailhead at 1,440 ft the Downey Creek trail runs about six easy forested miles to Sixmile Camp; after that the abandoned Bachelor Creek trail deteriorates badly. The first two mil…

camps_on_file.name: Cub Lake
camps_on_file.notes: Roughly 12 miles and about 3,900 ft of gain from the Downey Creek trailhead, reached by a steep switchbacking descent off the Bachelor Creek meadows and a walk around the north shore. Parties report anywhere from six hours to eleven getting here, which is a fair measure of how much the brush and the pack weight vary. I…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 4-day trip: ~33-35 miles and roughly 8,000-9,000 ft cumulative gain round trip, with one long alpine summit day off a high camp near Cub Lake/Itswoot Ridge.

days.title: Approach to Bachelor Creek
days.objective: Reach forest camp near the Bachelor Creek crossing (Sixmile Camp / Bachelor Flats)
days.note: Walk or bike the 8 closed miles of Suiattle River Road from the milepost 12 gate to the Downey Creek trailhead first. Hike the mostly gentle Downey Creek Trail to Sixmile Camp, then continue up the abandoned, brushy Bachelor Creek Trail to a flat camp near 4,500 ft. Expect slide-alder bushwhacking and a footlog crossin…

days.title: Over Cub Lake Pass to high camp
days.objective: Establish high camp on Itswoot Ridge or in the Cub Lake basin
days.note: Climb steep forest and meadow above Bachelor Flats, cross the snow slopes of Cub Lake Pass (~5,700 ft), and drop to Cub Lake or climb onto Itswoot Ridge to camp with views of the Dome/Chickamin Glacier. This is normally the crux navigation day if snow-covered.

days.title: Climb Sinister Peak
days.objective: Summit via the Southwest Route and return to high camp
days.note: An alpine-start glacier day: rope up and cross the Chickamin Glacier to the Dome-Sinister col, then climb the loose southwest gully and scramble the upper west ridge (Class 2-3) to the summit. Reverse the same line back to camp; parties reach the summit anywhere from late morning to early afternoon depending on party s…

days.title: Hike out to trailhead
days.objective: Descend from high camp to the Downey Creek trailhead
days.note: Break camp and reverse the full approach in one long push: back over Cub Lake Pass, down Bachelor Creek, and out the Downey Creek Trail, then the 8 closed miles of road to the milepost 12 gate. Most parties treat this as a single long descent day rather than splitting it again.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 4-day, roughly 29-mile round-trip backpack from Downey Creek Trailhead, gaining about 6,800 ft net to the 8,264 ft summit; the Bachelor Creek/Itswoot Ridge approach day is the crux of the logistics, and the summit itself is a short but airy Class 4-5 pitch with two 60m rappels to descend. Strong parties sometimes compress the return into a single long day instead of a second night at Sixmile Camp.

days.title: Approach to Sixmile Camp
days.objective: Reach Sixmile Camp on the Downey Creek Trail
days.note: Walk or bike the 8 closed miles of Suiattle River Road from the milepost 12 gate to the Downey Creek trailhead first. An easy, well-graded old-growth forest trail up the Downey Creek valley to the established Sixmile Camp, used as camp one by nearly every party heading for Spire Point or the Ptarmigan Traverse. Mellow …

days.title: Grind to Spire Col high camp
days.objective: Reach Spire Col via Bachelor Meadows, Cub Lake pass, and Itswoot Ridge
days.note: The crux logistics day: cross Bachelor Creek and fight through notoriously dense, wet brush on the Bachelor Creek Trail to Bachelor Meadows, cross the Cub Lake pass, then follow Itswoot Ridge (staying on talus left/west of the crest to dodge towers) to the Spire Col saddle at ~7,760 ft. Crampons typically go on around …

days.title: Summit Spire Point, hike back to Sixmile Camp
days.objective: Climb Spire Point via the southwest/southeast face, then descend to Sixmile Camp
days.note: A short, exposed technical climb from camp followed by a long hike back out. From the col, an ascending traverse onto the southeast face leads up slabs to the ridge crest, across to the west side, and along airy Class 3 ledges above 1,000+ ft of exposure to the base of the summit block, which goes at Class 4-5 to a hor…

days.title: Hike out to trailhead
days.objective: Return to Downey Creek Trailhead
days.note: A straightforward, mostly downhill walk back down the Downey Creek Trail and the 8 closed miles of road to the car at the milepost 12 gate, closing out the ~29-mile round trip from the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Spire Col bivouac
camps_on_file.notes: The col at 7,760 ft between Itswoot Ridge and the upper Dana Glacier, and the highest useful bivouac for Spire Point. Taking it saves an hour or more off summit morning on the Southwest Face and puts you above the section of snow that softens in the afternoon. It is fully exposed, cold, and windy, which is the trade. P…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip covering roughly 20 miles round trip and ~6,000 ft of net gain; the standard plan is one night in, a 6-hour summit round trip from Thunder Basin, and hike out the next day. Strong/fast parties occasionally compress it to a 2-day push, but the brushy unmaintained approach and loose, rappel-only summit pitch make the 3rd day worthwhile for most.

days.title: Approach to Thunder Basin high camp
days.objective: Establish camp in Thunder Basin below the SE col
days.note: Hike the White River Trail roughly 6 miles to Thunder Creek, then leave the maintained trail and follow the old, brushy sheep trail up the Thunder Creek drainage into the lower/upper basin. Route-finding through avalanche debris and brush makes this slower than the mileage suggests.

days.title: Summit push via the SE col, gully and chimney
days.objective: Climb the Southeast Route to the summit and return to camp
days.note: Alpine start up snow/talus to the col east of the summit block, then a loose gully and a broken, jam-crack chimney (class 4/easy 5th) to the top. Most parties rappel the chimney/face on descent rather than downclimbing since there are no fixed anchors — carry gear to build rap stations and leave slung horns/webbing.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the White River Trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach: descend Thunder Basin, rejoin the White River Trail at Thunder Creek, and hike the remaining 6 miles out to the trailhead.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day, 2-night trip: hike in to Goat Flats, a long technical day crossing the Queest-Alb Glacier and climbing class 4 to low-5th-class (5.1) rock to North Peak, then hike out; roughly 14.5 mi and 5,400 ft of cumulative gain overall.

days.title: Hike in to Goat Flats camp
days.objective: Reach Goat Flats camp
days.note: Walk or bike the 8 closed miles of FR 41 from the Canyon Creek bridge to Tupso Pass first. Same approach as the standard South Peak trip: Saddle Lake Trailhead through old-growth forest and Saddle Lake up to the meadows at Goat Flats. Carry the technical rack and glacier gear in addition to overnight kit since North Pe…

days.title: Technical summit day: North Peak
days.objective: Climb North Peak via the Queest-Alb Glacier and the Middle/North col
days.note: From camp, cross Tin Can Gap and drop roughly 400 ft onto the Queest-Alb Glacier before climbing back up about 1,000 ft to the col between Middle and North Peak. Rope up for sustained class 4 climbing with one low-5th-class (5.1) move in a summit chimney; exposure is constant.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead
days.note: Break camp at Goat Flats and retrace the trail down through Saddle Lake to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Goat Flats
camps_on_file.notes: Open subalpine meadow about two miles beyond the lake, and the default base for anything on Three Fingers — the lookout, the middle summit, or a look at the south face. From here the gap and the glacier are within a straightforward morning. It is also the honest fallback for a party that walked up hoping for a bunk in …

camps_on_file.name: Tin Can Gap high camp
camps_on_file.notes: The last flat ground before the glacier, roughly a mile short of the lookout, and the correct camp for a party that wants the summit block early and cold rather than soft. The maintained trail effectively ends here, so everything above is a bootpath, snow and the ladders. Its value is that it puts the glacier crossing …

camps_on_file.name: Saddle Lake
camps_on_file.notes: About two and a half miles in from the road end, in dense timber, and low enough that it is a contingency rather than a plan for anyone climbing. It matters for two reasons. First, the road: the Tupso Pass road has a long washout history and has at times been cut miles short of the trailhead, leaving parties to walk or…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day, 2-night trip shaped like the North Peak itinerary: hike in to Goat Flats, a technical South Face summit day, then hike out; roughly 14.5 mi and an estimated 5,100 ft of cumulative gain overall.

days.title: Hike in to Goat Flats camp
days.objective: Reach Goat Flats camp
days.note: Walk or bike the 8 closed miles of FR 41 from the Canyon Creek bridge to Tupso Pass first. Same shared approach as the other Three Fingers summits: Saddle Lake Trailhead up through old-growth forest and Saddle Lake to the meadows at Goat Flats.

days.title: Technical summit day: Middle Peak South Face
days.objective: Climb Middle Peak via the South Face
days.note: From camp, cross from Tin Can Gap onto the glacier to the foot of Middle Peak, then climb Middle Peak's South Face -- steep snow/scree giving way to class 3-4 rock, with a rope useful for the short exposed moves near the summit ridge.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead
days.note: Break camp at Goat Flats and retrace the trail down through Saddle Lake to the trailhead.

From here the gap and the glacier are within a straightforward morning. It is also the honest fallback for a party that walked up hoping for a bunk in …

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day, 1-night trip: ~4.5 mi and 3,000 ft up to Goat Flats camp on day one, then a long summit-and-hike-out day (~7.7 mi) with the final snow slope, rock scramble, and rebarred ladder to the historic lookout.

days.title: Hike in to Goat Flats camp
days.objective: Reach Goat Flats camp
days.note: Walk or bike the 8 closed miles of FR 41 from the Canyon Creek bridge to Tupso Pass first. From the Saddle Lake Trailhead, climb through old-growth forest past Saddle Lake and up into the alpine meadows of Goat Flats, the standard camp for a Three Fingers trip. Bears frequent the area, so hang or canister your food.

days.title: Summit push and hike out
days.objective: Tag the South Peak lookout, then pack out to the trailhead
days.note: Leave camp early for the push over Tin Can Gap and across the glacier to Camp Saddle: a steep snow slope (ice axe, crampons advisable even late season) followed by a rock scramble and a short rebarred ladder up to the 1930s fire lookout cabin. After the summit, break camp and hike the ~4.5 miles back out.

camps_on_file.name: Goat Flats
camps_on_file.notes: The main camp for the peak, an open subalpine meadow on a ridge crest a little over two miles beyond Saddle Lake and roughly two and a half miles short of the lookout, with a view west to Puget Sound. Bears work the area, so bring a canister or another way to secure food.

camps_on_file.name: Three Fingers Lookout
camps_on_file.notes: A 1930s fire lookout on the South Peak that climbers sleep in, reached by ladders with serious exposure — decide for yourself whether the final block is safe on the day. The door is never locked, but in winter and spring it can be frozen, swollen or buried, and the summit block itself is hard to climb then; summer is t…

camps_on_file.name: Saddle Lake
camps_on_file.notes: Two and a half miles in from Tupso Pass on a rough, root-bound forest trail — the first water and the first flat ground, but low and far from the mountain. Volunteers built a shelter at the meadow edge here in the early 1970s; no current source confirms it still stands or is usable, so do not plan on sleeping in it.

camps_on_file.name: Tin Can Gap
camps_on_file.notes: The last ground before the climbing starts: the Forest Service names it Tin Pan Gap, most climbers say Tin Can Gap, and it is where the route stops being a walk and starts needing equipment and judgement. accounts disagree on the distance in, from roughly six to eight miles, so do not plan a turnaround time off one fig…

trip_plan.totalNote: Hike 10.5 miles along Hozomeen Ridge to a camp near Monument 74, then climb the North Peak and hike out.

days.title: Hike to the Monument 74 camp
days.objective: Camp near 6,345 ft below Hozomeen
days.note: Start hiking mid-morning and cover the 10.5 miles and roughly 4,000 ft of trail to the Monument 74 area camp near 6,345 ft, which takes about 7 hours. Top off water at the last forest creeks before the ridge.

days.title: Climb the North Peak and hike out
days.objective: Summit via the northeast ridge, then walk out
days.note: Leave camp at first light and drop to the 5,800 ft saddle, then climb the cirque snowfields and northeast ridge to the summit. Return to camp, pack, and hike out.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day push of about 15 miles and 7,500 ft: trail to Hozomeen Lake and a brushy climb to a 4,900 ft bivy, a 16-hour summit day over the west notch and south face with a 5.6 bulge and three rappels, then a short exit.

days.title: Hozomeen Lake and bushwhack to bivy
days.objective: Reach a bivy near 4,900 ft in the west gully
days.note: Hike the 4-mile trail from the Willow Lake/Hozomeen Lake trailhead (1,650 ft) at Hozomeen Campground to the lake, go round the east shore, and push east through blowdown and brush past dry streambeds at 3,100 and 3,300 ft. The gully stream sits in a 50 ft canyon around 4,000 ft, so finding water access is the crux. Bri…

days.title: South Peak via west notch and south face
days.objective: Summit the South Peak and return to the bivy
days.note: Climb the gully's loose boulders and slabs to the 7,100 ft notch, cross toward the 6,900 ft saddle, then traverse three 35-40 degree snow patches to the col below the summit ridge. A 5.0 ramp, a Class 4 buttress and a 12 ft unprotected 5.6 bulge lead to the summit. Descend with a short rappel over the bulge, about 50 f…

days.title: Descend to Hozomeen Campground
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Descend the steep forest between the dry streambeds, cross Hozomeen Creek around 2,400 ft, and angle northwest to hit the trail at its midpoint. It took about 3.6 hours from camp to the cars.

trip_plan.totalNote: Four days: haul wall loads to a camp north of the peak, traverse to the base and climb the face over two days with a bivy, then hike out.

days.title: Haul loads to camp north of the peak
days.objective: Camp just north of Hozomeen
days.note: Hike 11-plus miles with wall loads to a camp just north of the peak.

days.title: Traverse to the base and start climbing
days.objective: Reach the wall and climb as far as light allows
days.note: Spend about 4.5 hours downclimbing gullies and traversing ribs to the base, then climb as far as light allows. The first ascent party reached the top of pitch 10 and bivouacked.

days.title: Finish the face and descend
days.objective: Top out and return to camp via the north side
days.note: Finish the last two pitches and the 100 ft summit ridge stroll, then descend the north side to camp.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Hike out to the trailhead.

trip_plan.totalNote: Three days on the Eldorado-Inspiration icecap climbing Eldorado, Austera, Primus, Klawatti and Dorado Needle from two high camps.

days.title: Climb to the Inspiration Glacier camp
days.objective: Camp on rock at the edge of the Inspiration Glacier
days.note: Hike and scramble from the Eldorado Creek trailhead up the boulder field and basins, then climb the Eldorado Glacier and camp on rock at the edge of the Inspiration Glacier. Climb Eldorado in the evening if time and conditions allow.

days.title: Austera, Primus and Klawatti
days.objective: Climb three peaks and camp at Klawatti col
days.note: Cross the Inspiration Glacier east and climb Austera and Primus via the Klawatti and North Klawatti glaciers. Climb Klawatti from the col camp on its south side.

days.title: Dorado Needle and descend to the car
days.objective: Climb Dorado Needle, then return to the trailhead
days.note: Climb Dorado Needle from the McAllister Glacier side, then return over the Inspiration and Eldorado glaciers and descend to the car.

camps_on_file.name: Inspiration Glacier high camp
camps_on_file.notes: Rock outcrops at the edge of the Inspiration Glacier below Eldorado's East Ridge. The standard base for Eldorado and the start of the traverse.

camps_on_file.name: Klawatti col
camps_on_file.notes: Rock tent sites on the col below the south side of Klawatti Peak with running water and big views; well placed for Klawatti, Austera and Primus.

camps_on_file.name: Eldorado Creek basin
camps_on_file.notes: Open basin above the boulder field; a lower camp for parties splitting the approach.

trip_plan.totalNote: A six-day north-to-south traverse from Cascade Pass to Downey Creek, camping at Kool-Aid Lake, Yang-Yang Lakes, White Rock Lakes (with a rest day) and Itswoot Ridge.

days.title: Cascade Pass to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Cross Cache Col to the Kool-Aid Lake bivouac
days.note: Hike the Cascade Pass Trail 3.7 miles to the pass, then go off-trail south and cross Cache Col on the Cache Glacier. Descend to the Kool-Aid Lake bivouac at about 6,100 ft; expect 4-6 hours and about 3,300 ft of gain.

days.title: Kool-Aid Lake to Yang-Yang Lakes
days.objective: Cross Red Ledge and Spider-Formidable Col
days.note: Cross the exposed Red Ledge below Art's Knoll (Class 3 scrambling) and climb the Middle Cascade Glacier to Spider-Formidable Col. Descend to the Yang-Yang Lakes bivouac; plan on 8-11 hours with about 2,500 ft of gain and loss.

days.title: Yang-Yang Lakes to White Rock Lakes
days.objective: Traverse Le Conte Ridge and Glacier
days.note: Traverse Le Conte Ridge and cross the Le Conte Glacier, which has crevasse hazards. Descend to the White Rock Lakes bivouac, the visual highlight of the route; plan on 7-11 hours with about 2,000 ft of gain and loss.

days.title: Rest day at White Rock Lakes
days.objective: Rest or take a peak day
days.note: Day 4 is an optional rest day or peak day at White Rock Lakes.

days.title: White Rock Lakes to Itswoot Ridge
days.objective: Cross the Dana Glacier past Spire Point
days.note: Ascend the Dana Glacier, crossing the bergschrund, then summit Spire Point (8,264 ft) or traverse below it on the east face. Descend to the Itswoot Ridge bivouac; plan on 8-10 hours with about 3,000 ft of gain.

days.title: Itswoot Ridge to Downey Creek
days.objective: Hike out to the Downey Creek Trailhead
days.note: Descend Bachelor Creek through forest and follow the trail out to the Downey Creek Trailhead. Plan on 8-12 hours.

camps_on_file.name: Kool-Aid Lake
camps_on_file.notes: Planned camp, and the standard first night on the traverse — the first place with water and flat ground after Cache Col. Sites sit on the lip of a steep slope that drops thousands of feet toward the valley, so pitch back from the edge in wind. The col above holds snow well into July and there is no water at the col its…

camps_on_file.name: Yang Yang Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: Planned camp, the usual second night, in heather meadow among granite boulders below the Le Conte Glacier. It is a low point on the traverse and melts out later than its elevation suggests — a party in late June found nothing bare and pitched on snow with running water alongside. Sheltered relative to the passes on eit…

camps_on_file.name: White Rock Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: Planned camp, the last true alpine camp and the one most parties would not skip, looking straight across at the icefalls of Dome and Sinister. Dry dirt bivy platforms are usable by late June, earlier than the lower camps. It is an open basin with nothing to hide behind: one party sat out roughly twelve hours of rain an…

camps_on_file.name: Cub Lake meadows / Itswoot Ridge
camps_on_file.notes: Planned camp, the last night for parties exiting south to Downey Creek, in heather meadow below Itswoot Ridge. Melts out late — a late-June party found the lake still largely frozen, the basin barely opened up, and a marginal perch near 6,200 ft below the basin that they would not recommend sleeping on until more snow …

campsite_pins.name: White Rock Lakes / South Cascade Glacier Col

days.title: Day 1
days.note: Approach via Easy Pass and Fisher Creek to a high camp (~6,700 ft) on Mesahchie's south shoulder

days.title: Day 2
days.note: Traverse Mesahchie-Katsuk-Kimtah-Cosho and descend to the Fisher Creek trail.

camps_on_file.name: Mesahchie basin, below the col
camps_on_file.notes: This is the base for Mesahchie and the usual first night of any Ragged Ridge traverse. From Easy Pass the line goes cross-country west-northwest, sidehilling on heather and tiresome scree at around six thousand eight hundred feet for roughly three hours to reach the basin below Mesahchie Col. It is not a trail and it i…

camps_on_file.name: Ragged Ridge crest bivy, south of Mesahchie Col
camps_on_file.notes: This is the higher and more committing of the two Ragged Ridge camps, about a mile west-northwest of Easy Pass. Two ways reach it: sidehill west at roughly six thousand eight hundred feet on heather and scree, or climb the grassy slope just past the pass to gain the crest near seven thousand two hundred feet and follow…

camps_on_file.name: Fisher Camp, Fisher Creek basin
camps_on_file.notes: Fisher Camp sits in the forested basin west of and well below Easy Pass, reached by carrying on over the pass and descending into Fisher Creek. It is the comfortable option and it is also the alternative approach to Kimtah that some parties prefer: rather than the long sidehill traverse along the south flank of Ragged …

trip_plan.totalNote: A 5-day trip from the Hannegan Pass Trailhead: two approach days to a 6,480' saddle camp, a big 10+ hour summit day on the North Buttress, and two days back out - roughly 45 miles round trip with about 12,000 ft of gain and the same loss.

days.title: Hannegan Pass to Brush Creek
days.objective: Reach a Chilliwack River Trail camp near Brush Creek
days.note: From the Hannegan Pass Trailhead climb about 4 miles to Hannegan Pass, then drop east past Boundary Camp into the Chilliwack valley, bearing right at the park boundary onto the Chilliwack River Trail. Continue past U.S. Cabin camp, cross the Chilliwack River by the cable car, and camp near the Brush Creek junction, abo…

days.title: Brush Creek to the high camp
days.objective: Reach the 6,480' saddle camp on Bear's NW ridge
days.note: Follow the Chilliwack River Trail about 5 more miles down-valley to the Bear Creek confluence (the camp there is closed). Ford Bear Creek and climb steep, brushy timber and then huckleberry and slide alder east to the meadows above Ruta Lake, then cross beneath Points 6592 and 6822, passing a rock rib, to the saddle ca…

days.title: Summit via the North Buttress
days.objective: Climb the North Buttress and tag the 7,931' summit
days.note: Descend a gully from camp to the toe of the North Buttress, then climb the glacier-couloir/buttress line to the summit before reversing the descent gully back to camp. This is the long day of the trip — most of it spent on 5th-class rock with some 3rd/4th-class terrain low and high on the route.

days.title: High camp to Brush Creek
days.objective: Descend to the Chilliwack River Trail and camp
days.note: Reverse the traverse to the meadows above Ruta Lake, descend the brush and timber to re-ford Bear Creek, and walk back up the Chilliwack River Trail to camp near Brush Creek (or push on toward U.S. Cabin or Copper Creek camp to shorten the last day).

days.title: Hike out over Hannegan Pass
days.objective: Return to the Hannegan Pass Trailhead
days.note: Recross the Chilliwack River by the cable car, climb back past Boundary Camp to Hannegan Pass, and descend the last 4 miles to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Meadow basin below the northwest-ridge saddle
camps_on_file.notes: The standard and effectively the only high camp for the buttress, in heather meadow a little below the notch on the northwest ridge, where scattered trees give some wind shelter and flat grassy ground. Reached by climbing roughly 3,000 ft out of the Bear Creek valley to treeline on a rough climbers' path through open f…

trip_plan.totalNote: Two days over Hannegan Pass and down the Chilliwack to a saddle camp near 6,480 ft, two days on the 21-pitch buttress with a bivy, and two days back out over Hannegan Pass.

days.title: Hannegan Pass to Brush Creek
days.objective: Camp on the Chilliwack River Trail
days.note: Hike over Hannegan Pass and down the Chilliwack River Trail to camp near Brush Creek, since the Bear Creek camp is closed.

days.title: Ford Bear Creek to the saddle camp
days.objective: Reach high camp near 6,480 ft
days.note: Ford Bear Creek and climb steep, brushy timber to the meadows above Ruta Lake, then traverse the divide to the high camp on the broad saddle near 6,480 ft. The two approach days cover roughly 21 miles and 6,500 ft of gain.

days.title: Start the Direct North Buttress
days.objective: Climb the lower buttress and bivy
days.note: Drop to the glacier remnant below the wall and tie in where the toe of the buttress meets the snow. Climb the 21-pitch buttress, which has historically taken about 2.5 days with a bivy on route.

days.title: Summit and descend to camp
days.objective: Finish the route and return to camp
days.note: Finish the buttress, leave the rack and rope near the top, and solo easy terrain to the summit. Descend snow slopes through cliff bands back to camp.

days.title: Hike back toward the Chilliwack
days.objective: Start the hike out
days.note: Break camp and start the roughly 21-mile hike back out over Hannegan Pass.

days.title: Hike out over Hannegan Pass
days.objective: Return to Hannegan Trailhead
days.note: Finish the hike out over Hannegan Pass to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Basin below the Bear Mountain saddle
camps_on_file.notes: The launching point for the north side of Bear Mountain, reached by leaving the Chilliwack valley trail and following a lightly marked line up the ridge toward treeline and then over into the basin. It is a long way in — most parties treat it as a second or third night rather than something reachable from the road — an…

camps_on_file.name: Hannegan Camp, below Hannegan Pass
camps_on_file.notes: The obvious staging camp for a party that drives up Ruth Creek late and wants the pass behind them early. Because it sits on the forest side of the divide, the paperwork is entirely different from everything down the far side — parking pass only, no Marblemount errand. Road conditions on FS 32 have been unreliable in r…

camps_on_file.name: Boundary Camp
camps_on_file.notes: Boundary sits just over Hannegan Pass at the line where Forest Service ground becomes national park, which is exactly why it trips people up: you park under a Northwest Forest Pass and then sleep under an NPS permit. With only three sites it books out on summer weekends, and a party arriving without a reservation has n…

camps_on_file.name: US Cabin Camp, Chilliwack River
camps_on_file.notes: A deep-forest valley camp rather than a climbing bivy, and its value is positional — it is roughly where a party bound for Bear Mountain or the peaks further up the drainage stops before leaving the trail. The lack of a food locker is worth planning around, because the neighbouring camps have them and it is easy to ass…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip: two long approach days (~8 mi / 3,500 ft each way, with a wet Class 3 step at Depot Creek Falls) bracket a shorter but loose, choss-prone summit day (~3.5 mi round trip, ~2,800 ft gain/loss, 3-5 hrs from Ouzel Lake camp); very fit parties occasionally push it car-to-summit-and-back in one very long day (~17+ mi, 6,000+ ft), but the standard plan uses a camp at Ouzel Lake.

days.title: Border approach to Ouzel Lake camp
days.objective: Establish camp at Ouzel Lake (5,700 ft)
days.note: Drive to the Depot Creek trailhead on Chilliwack Lake Road (BC side), then follow the old Depot Creek trail/climbers' path up through old growth, past a steep, wet, rooty headwall alongside Depot Creek Falls (the crux of the approach, with an exposed Class 3 rock step), before climbing a final steep pitch onto the outw…

days.title: Climb Mount Custer via the southwest slopes
days.objective: Summit Mount Custer (8,630 ft) and return to camp
days.note: From Ouzel Lake, scramble the cairned broken buttress southwest of the lake onto the Redoubt Glacier, cross it to the southwest basin below Custer's summit near 7,700 ft, climb to the notch just south of the summit at about 8,260 ft, pull through the short crux gully there, and follow the loose South Ridge to the top (…

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Depot Creek trailhead
days.note: Reverse Day 1 in full: down the steep path off the outwash plain, back down alongside Depot Creek Falls (care needed on the wet Class 3 step, now descending), through the old growth, and back across the border to the cars.

trip_plan.totalNote: Hike in to Ouzel Lake or Silver Lake, climb the South Side route to Rahm's summit and back to camp, then hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Ouzel Lake or Silver Lake
days.objective: Reach a camp below the peak
days.note: Hike in to Ouzel Lake (via Depot Creek, including a border crossing) or to Silver Lake (via the Silver Creek bushwhack) and camp.

days.title: Climb the South Side to Rahm's summit
days.objective: Summit Rahm and return to camp
days.note: Climb the South Side route to Rahm's summit, about 2 hours from Silver Lake or 3-5 hours from Ouzel Lake, and return to camp. Alternatively, continue on to Custer or Spickard.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Hike out.

trip_plan.totalNote: A standard 3-day trip: ~17 miles and ~6,400 ft round trip, with one night at Ouzel Lake camp and a long (10-12 hr) glacier/rock summit day in between; some parties extend to 4 days to also tag nearby Mount Spickard from the same camp.

days.title: Approach to Ouzel Lake camp
days.objective: Establish high camp at Ouzel Lake
days.note: Hike the Depot Creek Road washout and old trail up the Depot Creek valley, passing Monument 65 and climbing the steep, wet trail alongside Depot Creek Falls (an 8-ft slippery rock step near the top is the crux of the approach). Camp on the sandy, treeless benches at Ouzel Lake (~5,700 ft), the standard base for both Re…

days.title: Summit day via Redoubt Glacier / South Face
days.objective: Climb Mount Redoubt and return to Ouzel Lake
days.note: From camp, cross Depot Creek and scramble the broken buttress southwest of the lake to gain the Redoubt Glacier, then rope up for a mostly gentle glacier walk (a few crevassed/icy sections) around to the south side. Exit the glacier at the low point near the flying buttress (~7,800 ft), kick steps up a steepening snow …

days.title: Exit to trailhead
days.objective: Hike out to the vehicle
days.note: Break camp and retrace the Depot Creek trail past the falls and Monument 65 back down to the road washout / parking area. Guides suggest allowing at least 3 hours for the descent alone; with breaks it typically runs 4-5 hours car-to-camp in reverse.
